subsystems.name: Survey and prospecting instruments
subsystems.role: find and characterise a target body from a distance and up close.

subsystems.name: Autonomous guidance and navigation
subsystems.role: fly, land and work around a body with tens of minutes to hours of light-travel delay.

subsystems.name: Anchoring and movement system
subsystems.role: hold position against a body whose gravity is a millionth of Earth's.

subsystems.name: Excavation and handling
subsystems.role: loosen and collect loose regolith or harder rock in vacuum and low gravity.

subsystems.name: Processing plant
subsystems.role: turn raw material into something worth shipping — water, oxygen, metals.

subsystems.name: Transport and delivery
subsystems.role: move product to where it is used — a depot, a station or Earth.
parts: aeroshell and parachute for Earth return

buildSteps.title: Choose the target
buildSteps.detail: Asteroids are picked mainly by orbit: bodies reachable with about 5 km/s of velocity change are far cheaper to visit than those with huge ores but awkward orbits. Spectral type hints at composition — carbon-rich for water and organics, metallic for iron, nickel and platinum-group metals.

buildSteps.title: Prospect it
buildSteps.detail: Telescopes give only a rough type. A spacecraft uses spectrometers and radar to map composition, then a lander or hopper measures strength, porosity and buried ice. This is the step sample-return missions have already rehearsed.

buildSteps.title: Test extraction at small scale
buildSteps.detail: Sampling arms proved regolith can be grabbed in microgravity, and the MOXIE instrument on NASA's Perseverance rover electrolysed Martian carbon dioxide into a few grams of oxygen per hour in 2021–2023. Mining would scale that idea to tonnes.

buildSteps.title: Anchor and mine
buildSteps.detail: A miner must react against something to dig. Options include drilling anchors, harpoons, or simply using the spacecraft's own mass and thrusters to push a scoop into loose regolith while ejecta is captured.

buildSteps.title: Separate the product
buildSteps.detail: Carbonaceous material is heated in a sealed vessel so water and other volatiles boil off and are condensed; ice is then electrolysed into hydrogen and oxygen. Lunar regolith, roughly 40% oxygen by mass locked in oxides, can be reduced by molten-salt electrolysis or hydrogen reduction to release oxygen and metal.

buildSteps.title: Store and ship
buildSteps.detail: Products are stored as cryogenic liquids or compressed gas in tanks sized for the trip. Because returning mass to Earth's surface is so costly, the first customers would be in space: propellant depots and life-support for satellites and stations.

buildSteps.title: Build a market
buildSteps.detail: Mining only pays if something needs the product. The viable early loop is water to propellant at a depot, with metals used for in-space construction rather than shipped home.

prerequisites.why: communication delays of minutes to hours make joystick mining impossible; robots must decide for themselves.
oxygen from carbon dioxide and water from regolith have been shown in labs and one Mars instrument, never at production scale.
no machine has ever dug into an asteroid; abrasive dust and no reaction force defeat conventional designs.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap heavy launch and in-space propulsion
prerequisites.why: every kilogram of hardware must be launched or assembled in orbit, so cost per kilogram sets the whole economics.
national laws such as the US Commercial Space Launch Competitiveness Act of 2015 grant rights to extracted materials, but no international regime governs asteroid claims.
with no propellant depots or orbital construction at scale, there is nothing to sell water or metal to.

pathway.milestone: sample returns from near-Earth asteroids — JAXA's Hayabusa2 brought back about 5 grams from Ryugu in 2020, and NASA's OSIRIS-REx about 120 grams from Bennu in 2023
pathway.unlocks: ground-truth data on asteroid composition and the handling technology to collect regolith.

pathway.milestone: prospecting missions to metallic and ice-bearing bodies, such as NASA's Psyche spacecraft launched in 2023 and due at the metal-rich asteroid Psyche around 2029, plus lunar polar ice surveys
pathway.unlocks: maps of where valuable material actually is.

pathway.milestone: small robotic demonstrations that extract water or oxygen from lunar or asteroid material and store it
in-space propellant depots buying water-derived fuel
pathway.unlocks: the first paying market, and a reason to scale up mining.

pathway.milestone: commercial extraction of metals for orbital construction
pathway.unlocks: a genuinely off-Earth industrial economy, if launch costs and law allow.
